verses.text: So what should we say? Should we keep sinning so grace can increase?
Absolutely not! We died to sin—how could we keep living in it?
Don't you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
So through baptism we were buried with him into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father's glory, we too could live a new life.
If we've been united with him in a death like his, we'll also be united with him in a resurrection like his.
We know our old self was crucified with him so that sin's power over our bodies would be broken and we wouldn't be slaves to sin anymore.
Anyone who has died has been released from sin.
If we died with Christ, we believe we'll also live with him.
We know Christ was raised from the dead and won't die again. Death no longer rules over him.
The death he died, he died to sin once for all. The life he lives, he lives for God.
In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
So don't let sin rule your mortal body or make you obey its desires.

Don't hand over any part of yourselves to sin as a tool for wrongdoing. Instead, offer yourselves to God as people brought from death to life, and offer every part of yourselves to him as a tool for doing what is right.
Sin won't rule over you, because you're under grace, not under law.
So what then? Should we sin because we're under grace and not under law? Absolutely not!
Don't you know that when you offer yourselves to someone as obedient slaves, you're slaves of the one you obey—either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness?
Thank God! You used to be slaves of sin, but you obeyed from the heart the teaching you were entrusted with.
You've been set free from sin and have become slaves of righteousness.

I'm putting this in everyday terms because of your human limitations. Just as you once handed yourselves over as slaves to impurity and ever-increasing wrongdoing, now offer yourselves as slaves to righteousness, which leads to holiness.
When you were slaves of sin, you weren't committed to righteousness.
What did you gain from the things you're now ashamed of? Those things end in death.
But now you've been set free from sin and become God's slaves. The result is a life set apart for God, and the outcome is eternal life.
Sin pays its wages in death, but God's free gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
